description: A CSV, TSV or JSON-lines table, read beneath the server's root in one bounded pass. Give `file` (or `stdin`, the table as text) and one form: the shape (nothing else), rows (`select`, `where`, `order-by`), groups (`group`, `agg`, `sort`, `top`), a join (`join`, `on`), the type report (`report`), or `query`, a SQL subset that means the same as the flags. A mix is args.conflict; `explain` prints the plan and runs nothing. A typed condition or sort key (n:int) refuses a cell that is not of the type, an empty one too: keep it out first, `where` n != '' and n:int > 5. The answer is the tool's JSON document, a page of 1000 rows by default: `limit`, `from` and data.next.from page it. A refusal names a rule, a hint and a repair (retry is an argv to run, choose lists options, none says why). The full text of a property is the resource table://help/NAME; table://help/tool is the full description of this tool.

properties.select: Columns to return, comma-separated: header names or #N (1-based), in the order given; a repeat repeats the column. A comma, backslash or leading # in a name is written with a backslash before it.
properties.where: Row filter: COLUMN OP VALUE (OP is = != < <= > >= contains), COLUMN in (a, b), not (...), joined by and or by or; never both at one level (use parentheses). Text compares bytewise; COLUMN:int, :dec(N), :float, :date, :timestamp, :datetime compare as that type, and a cell that is not of it, an empty one too, is refused: n != '' and n:int > 5. A value with spaces is 'quoted'.
properties.group: Count rows by these columns, comma-separated (header names or #N), one row per distinct combination, in byte order unless sort says otherwise. NAME:int, :dec(S), :float, :date, :timestamp or :datetime groups by value; ts:timestamp@day (also @hour, @month, @year) by period.
properties.agg: What to compute (default count): count, or FUNCTION:COLUMN with FUNCTION sum, min, max, mean or distinct, comma-separated. Cells are read as exact integers (distinct: as text) unless COLUMN ends in :dec(S) or :float; mean:col@N rounds to N digits. With group, one row per group; alone, one row. Example: count,sum:bytes,max:bytes.
properties.sort: With group or agg: order the groups by one output column (count, an aggregate as printed such as sum:bytes, or a group column), with - before it for descending. Without it the groups are in byte order.
properties.top: Keep only the first N rows (after order-by) or groups (after sort); N at least 1; needs order-by, group or agg. limit and from page inside it.
properties.limit: The most rows or groups in the answer (default 1000, ceiling 1000000). A cut answer has truncated true and data.next.from, the value of from for the next page.
properties.order-by: Sort rows by keys, comma-separated: a header name or #N, - before it for descending, and :int, :dec(S), :float, :date, :timestamp or :datetime after it to compare by value (default bytewise, so 10 sorts before 9). Later keys break ties. Not with group or agg; rows are held up to max-sort-rows, so also use where or top.
properties.report: Describe each column's cells instead of returning rows: `types` (cells, empty, int, dec, float, other, and suggest, the smallest :int, :dec(S) or :float that reads every cell) or `dates`. select picks the columns, where keeps rows, limit and from page the columns. Not with group, agg, order-by, sort or top.
properties.format: json (default): one JSON document; csv: rows or groups as csv; jsonl: one JSON object per line; text: for a person, the shape only. Only json is a document: for the others a refusal is one line on standard error, and a non-zero exit means the output is a prefix.
properties.query: Ask in a SQL subset instead of flags: select COLUMNS | * | count(*) | sum(c) | min(c) | max(c) | mean(c) | count(distinct c), each optionally `as NAME`, [from 'FILE'] [where COND] [group by COLUMNS] [order by KEY desc] [limit N offset N]. COND: c = 'x', != <> < <= > >=, contains, in ('a', 'b'), not, joined by and or by or (not both at one level). Numbers: cast(c as int) or c::int. Not with select, where, group, agg, sort, order-by, rename, rows or report.
properties.rows: Every row with all its columns and no condition (select * and nothing else). Takes none of select, where, group, agg, order-by or report.
properties.explain: Print the plan the other properties (or query) resolve to, as one JSON line, and do not run it: only the file's header is read, and a plan the run would refuse before reading a row is refused as the run refuses it.
properties.input-format: How the input is read: csv (default), or jsonl (also ndjson): one JSON object per line, whose columns the `fields` property declares.
properties.fields: With input-format jsonl: the columns, as dotted paths, comma-separated (id,user.name,items.0.sku). A path with no value in a line is refused unless absent is empty.
properties.absent: With input-format jsonl: refuse (default) or empty, for a declared path that has no value in a line.
properties.max-json-nodes: With input-format jsonl: the most JSON nodes a line may hold (default 4096).
properties.discover: With input-format jsonl: report the paths and kinds of value the first lines hold, to choose `fields` from, instead of running a plan.
properties.join: The build side of a join: a second CSV file beneath the root. `file` (or stdin) is the probe side, streamed; this file is held in memory, counted in max-state-bytes. Needs `on`. Rows come in the probe's order. See join-type, join-prefix and join-where.
properties.on: With join: the key, 1 to 8 comma-separated pairs, each PROBE=BUILD (a column of file and one of the join file; header names or #N) or one NAME both files have. Cells are equal as text; end a pair with :int, :dec(S), :float, :date, :timestamp or :datetime to compare as that type (a cell that is not of it is refused).
properties.join-type: With join: inner (default), left (an unmatched probe row once, build cells empty), semi (probe rows that have a match), anti (probe rows that have none) or full (left, then each build row nothing matched, probe cells empty).
properties.join-prefix: With join: text put before every column name of the join file in the answer, so that files with a column of the same name can be joined (d_ makes id d_id). Without it a shared name is join.column-collision.
properties.join-where: With join: a where expression over the join file's own columns (no prefix), applied to its rows before they are held: the ON of a SQL join. In a left join a probe row left without a match is kept, where the same condition in `where` would drop it.
properties.max-join-rows: With join: the most rows the join may produce (default 10000000); one more is limit.too-many-join-rows.
properties.rename: Rename columns of the answer, comma-separated TARGET=NEW: TARGET is a label as printed (customer, sum:bytes) or #N (1-based), NEW the new label. Only the answer's labels change: where, group, agg and order-by keep naming header columns, and sort names the new label.
properties.join-input-format: With join: how the join file is read when it is not read as `file` is: csv, or jsonl (also ndjson).
properties.join-fields: With join and a JSON-lines join file: its columns, as `fields` declares them for `file`.
properties.join-delimiter: With join and a csv join file: its field separator, a comma, the word tab, or a semicolon.
properties.join-sorted: With join: declare that `file` and the join file are both in ascending order of the key, and run the join as a merge that holds one key of the join file at a time. The claim is checked (join.not-sorted). Not with query.
properties.max-state-bytes: The most bytes of group keys, distinct values, sorted rows or the join file kept (default 67108864, ceiling 1073741824), counted by a stated formula and not resident memory.
properties.threads: How many threads read the file (1 to 64, default 1) for rows and groups, on a file of at least parallel-min-bytes. The answer is the same bytes for any count; stdin is always one thread.
properties.file: The CSV file to read, a path relative to the server's root (absolute paths, `..` and symbolic links are refused); its first row is the header. Give exactly one of `file` and `stdin`.
properties.stdin: The table itself, as text, instead of `file`: give exactly one of the two. Read as `table -` reads standard input (a refusal names the path -); UTF-8 text, at most 1048576 bytes by default (--max-input), else mcp.input-too-large. A `query` must not name a source with `from` when this is given.
